2.title: Requirements

3.text:
npx claude-second-brain Or install globally for a shorter command (csb is an alias): npm i -g claude-second-brain
csb                    # same as: claude-second-brain The CLI will ask: Brain name — what to call this brain (default: my-brain) Git remote — optionally host your vault on GitHub (requires gh CLI) or Cloudflare Artifacts (requires a Cloudflare account + wrangler) Register qmd collections after install? — runs pnpm qmd:setup once dependencies are installed Install skills for which agents? — Claude Code plus any detected agent is preselected; see Install skills for any agent Every question is asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended. Creates the brain at ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/, registers it in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml, runs pnpm install (using your system pnpm 10+, or mise to fetch node + pnpm if it's missing), registers the qmd collections, installs the skills for the agents you picked, and runs git init.
3.title: Step 1 — Scaffold

4.text: cd ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain && pnpm qmd:reindex Generates local vector embeddings. First run downloads ~2GB of GGUF models — once.
4.title: Step 2 — Generate vector embeddings

5.text:
If you created a GitHub repo during setup, it's already pushed — skip straight to opening in Obsidian. If you skipped GitHub during setup, connect it now: git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main Open ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/ as a vault in Obsidian — the folder is already a valid Obsidian vault. The Git plugin is pre-configured — enable it and sync is automatic.
5.title: Step 3 — Open in Obsidian (and push to GitHub if not done)

6.text: Run npx claude-second-brain (or csb if installed globally) again to create additional brains. Each gets its own folder under ~/.claude-second-brain/ and its own isolated qmd index. The global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh) always operate on the default brain in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. The first brain created is set as the default automatically. See the CLI Reference for ls, use, rm, path, qmd, exec, skills, git-token, and doctor subcommands that manage and target specific brains.
6.title: Multiple brains

7.text: Edit anywhere — your agent on desktop, web or mobile. The vault is a plain git repo, so any agent that can clone it can work on it: run it locally, or use a cloud agent with GitHub access (Claude Code on the web and mobile, Codex cloud, Copilot coding agent, Cursor background agents, …) to ingest a source, run a query, or update a page from your phone. Read anywhere — Obsidian desktop and mobile. Open the repo as an Obsidian vault. The bundled .obsidian folder pre-configures obsidian-git — no setup required. Your wiki syncs automatically on every commit. For iOS: put the repo folder inside iCloud Drive — Obsidian Mobile picks it up natively. Browse anywhere — your git host. It's a plain git repo. On GitHub (or any host with a web UI), view and edit files directly in the browser at any time.
7.title: Access from anywhere

8.text: The claude-second-brain CLI creates and manages brains registered in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Run it via npx claude-second-brain, pnpm dlx claude-second-brain, or — if installed globally with npm i -g claude-second-brain — the shorter csb alias. All examples below use csb; substitute npx claude-second-brain if you haven't installed it globally.
8.title: CLI Reference

9.text:
Command Description csb Create a new brain (interactive). csb <name> Create a new brain named <name>, skipping the name prompt. csb ls List all registered brains. The default brain is marked with *. csb use <name> Set the default brain. csb rm [<name>…] Delete one or more brains. Interactive multi-select if no name is given. csb path [qmd|config|root] Print a path for the default (or named) brain. csb qmd [flags] <qmd args…> Run qmd against the default (or named) brain. csb exec [flags] -- <cmd…> Run a command inside the default (or named) brain's directory. csb skills [--agent <ids>] Install or update the wiki skills for any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …). csb git-token [<name>] Renew the git push/pull token for a Cloudflare Artifacts brain. csb doctor Verify your setup and suggest fixes. csb help [<command>] Show usage for a command. ls is also available as list; rm as remove; use as default or switch. Every subcommand accepts --help / -h for usage details: csb path --help
csb rm --help
csb qmd --help
9.title: Commands

10.text:
csb                     # interactive — prompts for name + remote
csb my-brain            # skip the name prompt
csb my-brain --agent claude-code,codex   # pick agents up front Options: --agent, -a <ids> — agents to install skills for, comma-separated or all. Also read from CSB_AGENTS. Without it, the CLI prompts (interactive) or uses Claude Code plus every detected agent (non-interactive). --copy — copy skills into each agent's folder instead of symlinking. See Install skills for any agent. CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none — icons in the git-remote picker. Real GitHub / Cloudflare logos (Nerd Font glyphs) are on by default in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty; set CSB_ICONS=nerd in other terminals if you use a Nerd Font. Otherwise emoji. Creates the brain at ~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/, runs pnpm install, pnpm qmd:setup, git init, and registers it in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. The first brain created is set as the default. During the interactive flow the CLI asks: Brain name — defaults to my-brain. Git remote — GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, or Skip. See GitHub and Cloudflare Artifacts. Repo name — only shown when a remote is selected; defaults to the brain name. Artifacts namespace — only shown for Cloudflare; defaults to default. Register qmd collections after install? — confirms running pnpm qmd:setup once dependencies are installed. Install skills for which agents? — multiselect; Claude Code and any detected agent are preselected. All questions are asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended. Long steps show a spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line. If pnpm 10+ is already on your PATH, it is used directly; otherwise the CLI installs mise (if needed) and runs mise install to fetch node + pnpm first. Set CSB_USE_MISE=1 to always use mise. The closing Next steps box shows how to open each agent you picked (claude, codex, cursor ., …). If the GitHub or Cloudflare remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, Next steps lists the fix, and the CLI exits 1.
10.title: Create a brain

11.text: csb ls Prints each registered brain with its path, creation date, and git remote. The default brain is shown in bold with a * marker.
11.title: List brains

12.text:
csb use work            # switch default to `work`
csb default work        # alias
csb switch work         # alias Rewrites the default = "…" line in ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Every subsequent command that resolves the default brain — path, qmd, exec, and the global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh) — uses the new default. Errors if the name isn't registered; run csb ls to see the available names.
12.title: Set the default brain

13.text:
csb rm my-brain                          # single brain, confirmation prompt
csb rm a b c                             # remove multiple by name
csb rm my-brain --yes                    # skip confirmation (remotes preserved)
csb rm a b --yes --delete-remote         # no prompts; also delete remotes
csb rm a b --yes --keep-remote           # no prompts; keep remotes
csb rm                                   # interactive multi-select picker Deletes each brain's directory under ~/.claude-second-brain/ and removes its entry from config.toml. If you remove the default brain and others remain, the first remaining brain becomes the new default. Interactive picker. When no name is passed, the CLI shows a multi-select list — press space to toggle a brain, a to toggle all, enter to confirm. Remote deletion. For each brain with a registered git_remote the CLI can also delete the remote repo: GitHub — runs gh repo delete <owner>/<repo> --yes (requires gh CLI with delete_repo scope). Cloudflare Artifacts — calls DELETE /v1/api/namespaces/<ns>/repos/<repo> using CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or a token fetched from wrangler auth token. Behavior depends on the flags: No flag + interactive — prompts per brain. --keep-remote — never prompts, never deletes remotes. --delete-remote — never prompts, always deletes remotes. -y / --yes with no remote flag — remotes are preserved (safe default). If a remote deletion fails (missing CLI, revoked token, etc.), the CLI prints the exact manual command and continues — the local directory and config entry are still removed. Flags: -y, --yes — skip the bulk confirmation prompt. --delete-remote — also delete remotes, no prompting. --keep-remote — skip remote deletion, no prompting.
13.title: Remove a brain

14.text:
csb path                        # default brain root
csb path qmd                    # default brain's qmd index
csb path config                 # ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml
csb path qmd --brain work       # a specific brain's qmd index Positional: root (default) — the brain's directory (e.g. ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain). qmd — the brain's qmd SQLite index (e.g. ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/.qmd/index.sqlite). config — the central config path. Ignores --brain. Flags: --brain <name> — target a specific brain instead of the default. --root / --qmd / --config — deprecated flag form. Still supported; prints a warning to stderr. Used by the global skills (/brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh) to resolve paths at call time so they work from any working directory.
14.title: Print a path

15.text:
csb qmd query -c wiki "distributed systems"
csb qmd --brain work search -c wiki "kafka"
csb qmd -- --brain literal-qmd-flag       # -- is optional; use to pass literal --brain to qmd Forwards all non-csb arguments to npx @tobilu/qmd, with INDEX_PATH set to the resolved brain's qmd index and cwd set to the brain's root. Flags: --brain <name> — target a specific brain instead of the default. -- — optional separator; everything after it is passed to qmd verbatim. Use only when you need to pass a literal --brain (or other csb-reserved flag) through to qmd.
15.title: Run qmd against a brain

16.text:
csb exec -- pnpm qmd:reindex
csb exec --brain work -- git status
csb exec -- ls Runs any command inside the resolved brain's directory with INDEX_PATH pre-set. Useful for vault-local scripts that assume you're cd'd into the brain root. Flags: --brain <name> — target a specific brain instead of the default. -- — required separator before the command to run.
16.title: Run a command inside a brain

17.text:
csb skills                          # prompt for agents, install/update skills
csb skills --agent codex,cursor     # non-interactive
csb skills --agent all --copy       # every supported agent, real copies
csb skills --list                   # supported agents + where they read skills The skills follow the Agent Skills format and are installed with the same layout as npx skills: Global skills (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh) are written once to ~/.agents/skills/<name>, with a .csb-version marker. Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Amp and Cline read ~/.agents/skills directly. Agents with their own folder get a symlink to the shared copy: ~/.claude/skills (Claude Code, honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills, ~/.config/goose/skills, ~/.kiro/skills, ~/.roo/skills, ~/.continue/skills, ~/.junie/skills, ~/.augment/skills. If a symlink can't be created, or with --copy, the skill is copied instead. Vault-local skills (brain-rebuild, lint) stay in the vault's .claude/skills/ and are copied — never symlinked, since the vault is a git repo — into each other selected agent's project folder (.agents/skills/, .windsurf/skills/, …) of the default brain, or the one named with --brain. Commit them to sync. Agents are detected by their config folder (e.g. ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, ~/.copilot). Upgrading from a release that installed only to ~/.claude/skills: run csb skills once — existing copies there are replaced with symlinks to ~/.agents/skills.
17.title: Install skills for any agent

18.text: csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print] Mints a new repo-scoped Artifacts token (90 days by default; --ttl 12h|30d|1y, max 1 year) and saves it as http.<remote>.extraHeader in the brain's .git/config, so git push / git pull work again. --print prints the token instead. See Cloudflare Artifacts.
18.title: Renew a Cloudflare Artifacts git token

19.text: csb doctor Checks for: Installed tools: gh (+ auth status), mise or pnpm 10+, wrangler (optional). A parseable ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. At least one registered brain. A resolvable default brain. For each brain: the path directory exists; the qmd_index file exists. Each global skill is installed in ~/.agents/skills at this release's version. Each failed or warning check prints a Fix: hint with the exact command to run. Exits non-zero on failures.
19.title: Verify your setup

20.text: Every command exits non-zero on failure (invalid brain name, missing config, failed doctor check, etc.) and writes the error to stderr.
20.title: Exit status

21.text: Your notes don't compound. This wiki does. The fastest way to start your personal knowledge base powered by Obsidian, your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and more), qmd, and git. npx claude-second-brain One command gives you a fully wired knowledge system: Your AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) ingests your sources and maintains a cross-linked wiki qmd powers local semantic search (vector + BM25) The scaffolded folder is your Obsidian vault — open it directly, with obsidian-git pre-configured for seamless sync Git (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, or any remote) is the source of truth — version history, anywhere access, and a backup you control You've been reading papers, articles, and books for years. Drop a source in, run /brain-ingest, and your agent reads it — extracts what matters, cross-links it to everything you already know, and files it. Ask a question six months later and get cited answers, not a list of files to re-read. Inspired by Andrej Karpathy's approach to LLM-powered knowledge management — share an "idea file" with an LLM agent and let it build and maintain your knowledge base.
21.title: claude-second-brain

22.text: This is not a RAG system. It's not a chatbot over your notes. It's an actively maintained, cross-linked wiki — five structured page types, YAML frontmatter, and a set of agent skills — usable from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, or any agent that supports Agent Skills — that run the whole thing. The schema (CLAUDE.md) is that idea file. Your agent reads it every session (other agents reach it through AGENTS.md).
22.title: How this is different

23.text: Tool Role Your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …) Reads sources, writes wiki pages, cross-links, flags contradictions qmd Local hybrid search (vector + BM25) across your entire wiki Obsidian Graph view, backlinks, mobile reading — offline, no extra sync Git (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, …) Source of truth — version history, your agent anywhere, Obsidian sync Everything is pre-configured. You bring the sources. Next: Get started in 3 steps →
23.title: The stack

24.text: A running record of every released version of claude-second-brain on npm. Newest releases first. For auto-generated notes and tags, see the GitHub releases page.
24.title: Ship log

25.text: Bug fixes for CLI argument handling, plus a test suite. Fixes: Brain names are validated before scaffolding. Names that are empty, . / .., or contain path separators, quotes or control characters are rejected, so a name can no longer escape ~/.claude-second-brain/ or corrupt config.toml. --brain now requires a value in path, qmd, exec, skills and git-token. Previously a bare --brain silently fell back to the default brain (so csb git-token --brain renewed the wrong brain's token). csb exec … -- <cmd> --help and csb qmd … -- … --help now pass --help through to the command after -- instead of printing csb's own help. Tests and CI: New pnpm test (node --test tests/*.test.js) covering brain-name validation, --brain parsing and help pass-through; a Test workflow runs it on pull requests and main. Docs: README and docs home link /brain-ingest, /brain-search, /brain-refresh, /brain-rebuild and /lint to their docs pages.
25.title: v1.2.3 — 2026-11-27

26.text: npm package metadata only. No CLI or template changes. Added npm keywords matching the GitHub repo topics (ai, amp, claude-code, codex, cursor, github, knowledge-base, knowledge-graph, knowledge-management, llm, obsidian, obsidian-vault, qmd, second-brain) so the package is searchable on npmjs.com. npm homepage now points to the docs site instead of the GitHub README, and bugs links to GitHub issues.
26.title: v1.2.2 — 2026-11-27

27.text: Maintenance release: security updates and a tokenless release pipeline. No CLI or template changes. Security: Refreshed dependencies to clear all Dependabot alerts (pnpm audit: 106 → 0). @clack/prompts is now ^1.9.0; transitive docs-site deps (hono, vite, mermaid, dompurify, …) resolve to patched versions, with pnpm overrides for toml, katex and @hono/node-server. Removed the stale package-lock.json; the repo uses pnpm only. Release pipeline: npm releases use trusted publishing (OIDC) from release-publish.yml with --provenance, so no NPM_TOKEN is stored in the repo. npm comes from mise.toml (11.21.2; trusted publishing needs 11.5.1+). v1.2.0 was the first release published this way. CI: Docs workflows install Playwright browsers from the locked version (1.65.1).
27.title: v1.2.1 — 2026-11-27

28.text: Works with any agent, not just Claude Code, plus a faster, unattended setup and first-class Cloudflare Artifacts git tokens. Existing installs: run csb skills once to move global skills from ~/.claude/skills to ~/.agents/skills (the old copies become symlinks). Agents: Skills install for any Agent Skills agent, with the same layout as npx skills: global skills are written once to ~/.agents/skills/<name> and symlinked into agent-specific dirs (~/.claude/skills, ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills, ~/.config/goose/skills, …). Supported: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Amp, Cline, Windsurf, Goose, Kiro CLI, Roo Code, Continue, Junie, Augment. Vault-local skills (brain-rebuild, lint) are copied into each selected agent's project skills dir (.agents/skills/, .windsurf/skills/, …). New --agent, -a <ids> (comma-separated or all) and CSB_AGENTS to pick agents; --copy to copy instead of symlink. Interactive setup preselects Claude Code plus every detected agent. New csb skills [--agent <ids>] [--copy] [--brain <name>] to add agents or update skills later, and csb skills --list to show supported agents and their skills dirs. New vaults ship an AGENTS.md that points Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other agents at CLAUDE.md. The Next steps box shows how to open each agent you picked (claude, codex, cursor ., …). Setup: All prompts, including the qmd-registration question, are asked up front; the rest runs unattended. Long steps show a live spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line. If pnpm 10+ is on your PATH, it's used directly; otherwise the CLI installs mise and fetches node + pnpm. CSB_USE_MISE=1 forces mise. The git-remote picker shows GitHub / Cloudflare logos as Nerd Font glyphs in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty, emoji elsewhere. Override with CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none. If the remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, the problem and fix are listed in Next steps, and the CLI exits 1. Cloudflare Artifacts: Switched to the account-scoped REST API (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…); the old artifacts.cloudflare.net/v1/api host is no longer used. Set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID when your login can see more than one account. A deleted or inactive namespace is recreated automatically before the repo is created. Setup now saves a 90-day git token in the vault's .git/config (http.<remote>.extraHeader), so git push / git pull and obsidian-git just work. No more 24-hour token to copy. New csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print] renews it (default 90 days, max 1 year), replacing the manual curl renewal. Other: csb doctor accepts system pnpm 10+ in place of mise and checks that the global skills in ~/.agents/skills match the installed release. README, docs and package description say "any agent" and "git" (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, or any remote) instead of Claude Code and GitHub only. "Claude reads it" and similar wording is now agent-neutral, and "Access from anywhere" covers any local or cloud agent and any git host.
28.title: v1.2.0 — 2026-11-27

29.text: CLI UX pass. Every addition is non-breaking — the -- in csb qmd -- … and the path --qmd / --config / --root flag form continue to work, with a stderr deprecation notice on the flag form. CLI: Added csb use <name> (aliases default, switch) to set the default brain without editing ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml. Runs the same header-rewrite path as csb rm. Added csb exec [--brain <name>] -- <cmd…> — runs any command inside the resolved brain's directory with INDEX_PATH pre-set. csb qmd now delegates to the same helper. Added csb doctor — checks for gh (+ auth), mise, wrangler, the central config, each brain's path and qmd_index, and whether the default brain resolves. Prints a Fix: hint under each failed check. csb path now accepts positional subcommands: csb path [qmd|config|root]. The --qmd / --config / --root flag form still works with a stderr deprecation warning. Every subcommand routes --help / -h to its own topic help. csb help <command> also prints per-command help. Top-level help shows the config path and current default brain. csb rm gained --delete-remote and --keep-remote for scripting. Under -y with neither flag, remotes are preserved (safe default). resolveBrain() error now points to csb use <name> as the fix.
29.title: v1.1.0 — 2026-04-19

30.text: First major release. Brains now live at ~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/ (not the repo root), and global skills resolve paths at call time via new CLI subcommands instead of baked-in paths. Existing single-brain installs: re-run npx claude-second-brain <name> to migrate. Legacy active = … in config.toml is auto-rewritten to default = …. CLI: Added claude-second-brain path [--brain N] [--root|--qmd|--config] and claude-second-brain qmd [--brain N] -- … subcommands. The global skills now resolve paths at call time via these commands instead of having absolute paths baked in at scaffold time. Added claude-second-brain rm [<name>…] with multi-select (space to toggle) and a follow-up prompt to delete the git remote. config.toml's active field renamed to default. Existing configs with active = … are still read transparently and rewritten to default = … on the next write. Global skills (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh) now ship with a .csb-version sidecar file. Re-running npx claude-second-brain <name> detects version mismatches and prompts before overwriting; CSB_SKIP_SKILL_UPDATES=1 disables the prompt. npx claude-second-brain now auto-registers qmd collections during scaffold — no manual /setup step needed afterwards. Added csb as a bin alias. After npm i -g claude-second-brain, both claude-second-brain and csb are available globally. Skills: Removed /setup and /qmd-cli — their responsibilities are absorbed by create.js (auto-registration) and /brain-refresh / the csb qmd proxy respectively. Added /update-workflows to audit pack-test.yml drift against current repo state. Split /release into /package-release (version bump + PR) and an orchestrator /release that additionally runs /update-workflows and /update-docs. Refactors: Removed the __QMD_PATH__ and __CSB_CONFIG__ placeholder substitutions. scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts now compute the index path from import.meta.url; CLAUDE.md and vault-local skills use a relative .qmd/index.sqlite path. patchVault() now only substitutes __BRAIN_NAME__ in template/README.md. Global skills ship unmodified from the template. Fixes: writeConfig() now writes default = … when upserting into a pre-existing empty or default-less config.toml. Previously a zero-byte config.toml blocked the field from being written and left CLI subcommands unable to resolve a default brain. pnpm qmd:setup failures during scaffolding now surface captured stderr (last ~10 lines) instead of a generic "failed" message. template/scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts wrap their bodies in try/catch that prints a tagged error with vault + db paths and exits 1, replacing silent unhandled rejections. resolveBrain() errors now list available brain names and include a fix hint. Docs: Getting-started, per-skill docs, and vocs sidebar updated to reflect the 5-skill surface (brain-ingest, brain-search, brain-refresh, brain-rebuild, lint). Documented rm multi-select and remote-deletion prompts. /setup skill reference removed from quick-start in favor of pnpm qmd:reindex.
30.title: v1.0.0 — 2026-04-19

31.text: Features: Added Cloudflare Artifacts as an alternate Git remote option during npx claude-second-brain setup. Global Claude skills are installed right after pnpm install, before git init. Install path is shown with ~/... notation. qmd index prompt placeholder and default value display ~/... instead of the full home directory path. 42.text: Refresh the qmd index. Re-scans all collections for new or changed files and regenerates vector embeddings. Run after a bulk ingest session or manual edits to the wiki. Pass force to re-embed every chunk — useful after changing the embedding model. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-refresh). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md.
42.title: /brain-refresh

43.text: Ingest a new source into the wiki. Drop a file into raw-sources/articles/, raw-sources/pdfs/, or raw-sources/personal/, then run /brain-ingest. Your agent will: Read the source in full. Summarize it in 3–5 bullets and ask you what matters most. Create a wiki/sources/[slug].md page with abstract, key claims, notable quotes, and your synthesis note. Update or create topic/entity pages that the source touches, integrating it as prose (not copy-paste) with source attribution. Flag contradictions with [!WARNING] callouts on any page where the new source disagrees with existing claims. Log the ingest in wiki/log.md. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-ingest). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md.
43.title: /brain-ingest

44.text: The wiki ships with a set of Agent Skills that cover the full workflow, and they work in any agent that supports skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. No manual prompting, no copy-pasting.
44.title: Skills

45.text: /brain-ingest — Drop a file into raw-sources/. Your agent summarizes the source, creates a wiki/sources/ page, updates related topic pages, and flags contradictions. /brain-search — Ask anything. Your agent runs hybrid search, reads the most relevant pages, and writes an answer with inline [[wiki/page]] citations. /lint — Health-check the wiki. Surfaces orphan pages, broken links, unresolved contradictions, and data gaps.
45.title: Daily workflow

46.text: /brain-refresh — Re-scan the vault and regenerate vector embeddings for new or changed files. /brain-rebuild — Destructive. Redesigns the qmd schema, drops the old index, and rebuilds from scratch. Use only when the current structure no longer fits how you search.
46.title: Maintenance

47.text:
The skills follow the Agent Skills format, so they work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. /brain-ingest, /brain-search, and /brain-refresh install globally during setup — once to ~/.agents/skills/, with symlinks from agent-specific folders like ~/.claude/skills/. /brain-rebuild and /lint live inside the vault at .claude/skills/ and are copied to .agents/skills/ and other agents' folders for the agents you pick. To install for more agents later, or after upgrading the CLI: npx claude-second-brain skills --agent codex,cursor,github-copilot See Install skills for any agent for the full layout. To pull in improvements from the latest template: # Install or update all 5 wiki skills
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills -a claude-code -y

# Or update a specific skill
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills --skill brain-ingest -a claude-code -y Once installed via npx skills, future updates are a single command: npx skills update -a claude-code
47.title: Install or update skills

48.text: Destructive. Redesign the qmd schema from scratch. Use only when the current collection/context structure no longer fits how you search — for example, when the wiki has grown into new domains that deserve their own collections. What it does: Analyzes the current wiki. Proposes new collections and contexts. Waits for your approval before any destructive action. Patches scripts/qmd/setup.ts, drops the old index, and rebuilds embeddings from scratch. Scope: vault-local, installed at .claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. .agents/skills/brain-rebuild). Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md.
48.title: /brain-rebuild

49.text: Query the wiki to answer a question. Runs hybrid search (vector + BM25) across the entire wiki, reads the 2–5 most relevant pages, and synthesizes an answer with inline [[wiki/page]] citations. Flags gaps where the wiki has no coverage. If the answer pulls together multiple pages in a novel way, it offers to file it as a permanent wiki/qa/[slug].md entry — so the synthesis compounds next time. Scope: global skill, installed once at ~/.agents/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/brain-search). Paths resolve at call time via npx claude-second-brain path and npx claude-second-brain qmd — both read ~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml to find the default brain. Source: template/.claude/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md.
49.title: /brain-search

50.text: Health-check the wiki. Reports on: Orphan pages — wiki pages with no inbound [[links]]. Unresolved contradictions — pages with [!WARNING] Contradiction callouts that haven't been resolved. Stale claims — claims superseded by newer sources. Missing pages — concepts/entities referenced by [[links]] that lack their own page. Broken links — wikilinks pointing to files that don't exist. Data gaps — important topics that lack source coverage; suggests specific sources to investigate. Applies fixes where safe and flags everything else for your review. Appends a summary to wiki/log.md. Scope: vault-local, installed at .claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. .agents/skills/lint). Source: template/.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md.
50.title: /lint

51.text: Cloudflare Artifacts is a git-compatible object storage remote. It's a good choice if you don't want to use GitHub — your vault data stays on Cloudflare's infrastructure and never touches GitHub.
51.title: Cloudflare Artifacts remote

52.text: A Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (required for Artifacts) Either wrangler login (the CLI runs it for you and requests artifacts:write), or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN set to an API token with Artifacts › Read and Artifacts › Edit If your login can see more than one account, set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID (or pick it when prompted) wrangler CLI — if not installed, the setup wizard falls back to npx wrangler automatically
52.title: Prerequisites

53.text: When you run npx claude-second-brain and select Cloudflare Artifacts as your remote, the CLI handles everything: Checks wrangler auth (logs you in and requests the artifacts:write scope if needed) Resolves your account ID and creates a new Artifacts repo via the Artifacts REST API (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…) Runs git remote add origin <remote-url> Pushes the initial commit Mints a 90-day git token and saves it in the vault's .git/config, so git push / git pull just work
53.title: Setup (automatic)

54.text:
Artifacts git tokens expire (csb mints them for 90 days; Cloudflare allows up to 1 year). When git push or git pull starts failing with an auth error, renew it: csb git-token            # default brain
csb git-token my-brain   # a specific brain This mints a new repo-scoped token with your wrangler login (or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and stores it for the brain's remote as http.<remote>.extraHeader in the vault's .git/config — local only, never committed. Plain git push / git pull (and obsidian-git) work again until it expires. Options: --ttl <duration> for a different lifetime (seconds, or 12h, 90d, 1y; max 1 year), --read for a read-only token, --print to print the token instead of saving it (e.g. for another machine: git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer $(csb git-token --print)" pull).
54.title: Renewing the git token

55.text: During setup, the CLI asks for an Artifacts namespace (default: default). Namespaces scope repos within your Cloudflare account — useful if you manage multiple projects. For personal use, the default is fine.
55.title: Namespace

56.text: If the repo can't be created or the first push fails, the CLI still creates the brain locally but says so in a warning, lists the fix in Next steps, and exits non-zero. A 403 / Authentication error usually means Artifacts isn't enabled on the account (Workers Paid plan), the token is missing the Artifacts permission, or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID points at another account. A 404 / Namespace is not active means the namespace was deleted; the CLI recreates it and retries automatically, and if that still fails, wait a minute (deletion can take a moment to finish) or pick another namespace. Fix it, then csb rm <name> and re-run, or add any other git remote by hand.
56.title: If setup fails

58.text:
┌─────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐

58.title: The ingest loop, zoomed in

59.text:
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema. Your agent reads this every session.
├── raw-sources/           ← Your raw inputs. The agent never modifies these.
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/

│   └── qa/

59.title: Directory layout

60.text: GitHub is the default Git backend for claude-second-brain. Your vault is stored as a private GitHub repository — you get version history, access from any device, and Obsidian mobile sync via the bundled Git plugin.
60.title: GitHub remote

61.text: A GitHub account gh CLI — used for authentication and repo creation during setup
61.title: Prerequisites

62.text: When you run npx claude-second-brain and select GitHub as your remote, the CLI handles everything: Checks gh auth status — runs gh auth login if not authenticated Creates a private repo: gh repo create <name> --private --source=. --remote=origin --push Pushes the initial commit
62.title: Setup (automatic)

63.text:
If you skipped GitHub during setup, or gh wasn't installed, connect it manually: # With gh CLI
gh repo create my-brain --private --source=. --remote=origin --push

# Without gh CLI
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main
63.title: Manual setup

64.text: The vault includes a pre-configured .obsidian/ folder with obsidian-git settings. Enable the plugin in Obsidian → Community plugins and it will auto-commit and push on a schedule. For iOS: place the repo folder inside iCloud Drive — Obsidian Mobile picks it up natively and obsidian-git handles sync.
64.title: Syncing from Obsidian

65.text: The authoritative schema lives in CLAUDE.md — your agent reads it at the start of every session (agents that look for AGENTS.md are pointed to it). This page is a readable summary.
65.title: Wiki schema

66.text: Type File Purpose overview wiki/overview.md Evolving high-level synthesis topic wiki/[concept].md A concept, domain, or idea entity wiki/[name].md A person, tool, company, or project source-summary wiki/sources/[slug].md One page per ingested source qa wiki/qa/[slug].md Filed answers to notable queries Plus two admin pages: wiki/index.md (master index) and wiki/log.md (running activity log).
66.title: Page types

67.text:
Every wiki page has YAML frontmatter: ---
type: overview | topic | entity | source-summary | qa | admin
tags: [tag1, tag2]
sources: ["[[wiki/sources/source-slug]]"]
related: ["[[wiki/related-page]]"]
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
67.title: Frontmatter

68.text: File names — kebab-case, all lowercase. machine-learning-ops.md, not MachineLearningOps.md. Links — always Obsidian [[wikilinks]] for internal cross-references. Full paths from vault root: [[wiki/distributed-systems]]. Sections — ## for top-level, ### for subsections. Contradictions — flagged with a > [!WARNING] Contradiction callout. Both claims and their sources are stated. Uncertainty — claims the model isn't sure about are marked with [?] inline.
68.title: Naming conventions

69.text:
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema
├── raw-sources/           ← Immutable raw inputs
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/
└── wiki/                  ← Agent-owned knowledge base
    ├── index.md
    ├── log.md
    ├── overview.md
    ├── sources/
    └── qa/
69.title: Directory layout

70.text: Nothing in raw-sources/ is ever modified — they are immutable raw inputs. Only wiki/ is owned by the agent; the rest of the vault is untouched. wiki/log.md is append-only, never overwritten. One source summary per ingested source in wiki/sources/ — never merged. Every wiki page has frontmatter with at least type and updated. Cross-link aggressively — if a topic has (or should have) a page, link it with [[wiki/page]]. Pages are synthesis, not transcription.
70.title: Hard rules
